findings.summary: Targeted MCP HTTP E2E tests selected the first viewer window, which could be an empty viewer when another DocuLight instance owned the fixed Windows IPC pipe.
findings.resolution: Added getViewerContaining() and switched DOM assertions in TC-20, TC-23, and TC-24 to wait for the viewer containing expected rendered text.

findings.summary: A user-installed DocuLight.exe can own the fixed named pipe during local E2E runs.
findings.resolution: No product change in Wave 1. The targeted E2E assertions now avoid relying on the pipe-backed list_viewers result for renderer DOM selection.

findings.summary: A per-file read/index failure during rebuild could produce and commit a partial replacement index instead of preserving the last committed index.
findings.resolution: Rebuild now aborts before consolidate/save when any file fails and restores the previous committed in-memory index. test/test-search-engine-lifecycle.js now verifies partial index/read failure rollback and failed file diagnostics.

findings.summary: MCP update_markdown with filePath could skip save/dirty handling because the shared save helper only considered lastRenderedContent or params.content.
findings.resolution: filePath updates now retain canonical rendered content in the window entry, and saveMcpUpdatedContent can persist source file updates. test/test-mcp-http-save-parity.js covers filePath update persistence.

findings.summary: Reviewer evidence gaps remained for stdio/HTTP shared fixture parity, required parameter/enum parity, and Settings status payload fields.
findings.resolution: Tests now cover shared stdio/http helper fixture parity, parsed source/bundle tool-name parity, query requirement and docType enum checks, and direct Settings indexing status payload fields.

findings.summary: SRS trace links still described pre-implementation negative gaps after the requirements were moved to implemented.
findings.resolution: Trace tables for FR-DOC-018, IR-APP-010, IR-MCP-013, and OPS-ARCH-004 now reference current implementation and test evidence. Strict SpecKiwi validation passes with 0 warnings.

findings.summary: HTTP open_markdown could still save frontmatter-only project/docType documents under default/note because save path metadata depended on explicit params and real WindowManager did not store project/docType metadata.
findings.resolution: WindowManager now stores project/docType metadata from explicit params or document frontmatter, HTTP and stdio open_markdown pass WindowManager-resolved metadata to saveMcpFile, and test/test-mcp-http-save-parity.js covers the frontmatter-only {project}/{type} save path.

verification.result: Nash A+, Tesla A+, Anscombe follow-up A+ after W1-RFL-007
